name: Question 10
problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x-5=y \\ y=2x+3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
First, we organize the system so that it’s in the correct order and  both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x-y=5 \\ -2x+y=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we organize the system so that it’s in the correct order and both x and y appear in each equation:

{x−y=5−2x+y=3

Now, we can write the system in the form Ax=b, where

A=[1−1−21]

is the coefficient matrix,

b=[53]

is the column vector of constants, and

x=[xy]

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation Ax=b becomes

[1−1−21][xy]=[53].
